rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Organic chemistry is the chemistry of carbon compounds** — hydrocarbons and their derivatives, with carbonates, carbides, cyanides and the carbon oxides left to inorganic chemistry by convention. The subject was born when **Wöhler (1828)** converted the inorganic salt **ammonium cyanate (NH₄OCN) into urea (NH₂CONH₂)**, destroying **Berzelius's vital force theory** and proving one chemistry for the living and the…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Wöhler: NH₄OCN → NH₂CONH₂ (urea) - Both have molecular formula CH₄N₂O (isomerism) - Combustion: CₓHᵧ + O₂ → x CO₂ + y/2 H₂O

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ All atoms are identical in an element. ✅ Isotopes have same protons but different neutrons.  ·  ❌ Atoms are indivisible. ✅ Atoms consist of protons, neutrons, and electrons.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Specialized insight for 01 introduction to organic chemistry and organic compounds.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Ammonium cyanate into urea*** — one gentle heating rearranged an inorganic salt into the organic molecule of urine: same composition (CH4N2O), different compound — vitalism refuted and isomerism introduced in a single experiment.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ Electrons orbit in fixed paths like planets. ✅ Electrons exist in probability clouds (orbitals).  ·  ❌ Heisenberg uncertainty means we cannot measure position and momentum precisely simultaneously — not that we lack good instruments.

rows.text: Definition = carbon compounds (minus carbonates/carbides/cyanides/CO-CO2). Wohler 1828: NH4OCN -> urea, killed vital force theory. Property list: covalent, low mp/bp, flammable, non-conductor, organic-solvent soluble, isomerism, slow.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The vital force theory died in one flask: the same atoms obey the same chemistry inside and outside a living cell — Wöhler's urea is the boundary stone of the whole subject.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Organic chemistry = chemistry of carbon compounds (hydrocarbons + derivatives); excludes carbonates, bicarbonates, carbides, cyanides, CO/CO2 (inorganic by convention). Vital force theory (Berzelius): organic compounds need living force; refuted by Wohler 1828: NH4OCN (inorganic) heated -> NH2CONH2 urea (organic) —…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: More organic compounds are known than compounds of all other elements put together — tens of millions — because carbon catenates into chains and rings and every chain can carry functional groups.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ de Broglie wavelength applies only to light. ✅ All matter has wave nature; detectable mainly for small masses like electrons.  ·  ❌ Quantum number l can be any integer. ✅ l ranges from 0 to n−1.  ·  ❌ Magnetic quantum number ml determines energy. ✅ ml determines orbital orientation, not energy (in absence of magnetic field).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Spin quantum number ms can be ±½ or any value. ✅ ms is always +½ or −½.  ·  ❌ Aufbau principle means filling from bottom to top of the diagram. ✅ Fill lowest-energy orbitals first: 1s→2s→2p→3s→3p→4s→3d→4p→...  ·  ❌ Pauli exclusion allows two electrons per orbital with any spin. ✅ Two electrons in same orbital must have opposite spins.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Hund's rule means pair electrons before spreading. ✅ Electrons fill degenerate orbitals singly first with parallel spins.  ·  ❌ The mole is just a number like dozen. ✅ 1 mole = 6.022×10²³ particles (Avogadro constant) — a bridge between atomic and macroscopic scales.  ·  ❌ Molar mass and molecular mass are the same thing. ✅ Molecular mass is in amu; molar mass is in g/mol — numerically equal but different units.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Limiting reagent is the reactant with smallest mass. ✅ Limiting reagent is the one that produces the least product (determined by moles, not mass).  ·  ❌ % yield can exceed 100%. ✅ % yield >100% indicates impure product or incomplete drying.  ·  ❌ Molarity and molality are the same. ✅ Molarity = mol/L solution (changes with T); Molality = mol/kg solvent (temperature-independent).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ A strong acid completely ionizes in water. ✅ Strong acids (HCl, HNO₃, H₂SO₄) are ~100% ionized; weak acids partially ionize.  ·  ❌ pH can be negative. ✅ pH < 0 is possible for concentrations >1M (e.g., 2M HCl has pH ≈ −0.3).  ·  ❌ Kc changes when concentration changes. ✅ Kc is constant at constant temperature; only temperature changes K.
